# Services that were removed on purpose.
#
# `watch-agent.sh` reports a service that logged in the last seven days and
# nothing in the last twenty-four hours. A service somebody deliberately removed
# looks exactly like a dead runner from inside Loki, because the difference
# between the two is an intention and an intention is not in the logs. This file
# is where the intention is written down.
#
# One service per line: name, the date it was removed, and why. Everything after
# the first field is for a reader; only the first is matched. A line starting
# with `#` is a comment.
#
# **Append to this only when a service is taken away on purpose, and never to
# quieten a service that ought to be running.** The check refuses a hardcoded
# list of expected services for a good reason — it would be wrong the first time
# one was added, and it would be a file somebody had to edit on the happy path.
# This is the opposite of that list and its normal state is empty: forgetting an
# entry here costs one issue closed with a sentence, while quietening a real
# service costs an outage nobody is told about.
#
# A line stops doing anything seven days after its date, because by then the
# service has not logged inside the window either and the check has stopped
# looking at it. `gather` says so in the run log, and the line can be deleted.

umami	2026-08-06	kolonie-website#43 — the maintainer decided PageSense stays and Umami is not wanted; removed from the host in kolonie-infra 83541e7
vikunja-reference	2026-08-28	kolonie-infra#252 and kolonie-infra#253 — torn down on purpose; a quiet alarm here would be the measurement without the intention
